ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: “Bah!” is a sharp voiced exclamation recorded as rebuke, interruption, or closing cry, often immediately before a blow or descent from the seat.
EvidenceBody: An abrupt exclamation, conventionally rendered “Bah!” In the Chan record it is a spoken action: named Chan speakers insert it before a rebuke, use it alone as an answer, or direct it at a named interlocutor. The Stove-Breaker strikes the stove and says “Bah! This stove is only made of mud and tiles” ; Danyuan says “Bah! Foolish fellow! Who is in the well?” ; and one record answers “What is the Way?” simply with the exclamation before ordering the unnamed questioner away. Its Chan deviation is this regular placement inside encounter dialogue as an answer or verbal blow, rather than merely narrative punctuation. The corpus gives the sound no further lexical gloss.
